requirements.title: No analytics or marketing processing before consent
observations: 1 analytics/marketing cookie(s)/script(s) fired before any consent interaction.
requirements.description: Analytics and marketing cookies and scripts do not run before the visitor has given consent.
requirements.criteria: Met: no request or cookie matching a known analytics or marketing service was observed before any consent interaction. Partially Met: only unclassified third-party items fired before consent. Not Met: at least one known analytics or marketing request or cookie was observed before consent. Unable to Verify: no pages scanned, a framed wrapper, or no three-state consent record.
requirements.expected_evidence: Before-consent observations (requests and cookies, with the page) from a scan pass made before any banner interaction.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 1 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.why_it_matters: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action (Act s.6(1)). Processing that starts before that choice has no consent behind it unless another ground in the Act applies.
requirements.remediation: Load analytics and marketing tags only after the visitor accepts: configure the consent tool to block them by default, or start them from its accept callback. Identify each unclassified item and treat it as non-essential unless it is needed for the service the visitor asked for.
requirements.verification: Re-scan. The Before Consent state should show no analytics or marketing requests or cookies, and they should appear only after Accept.
requirements.applicability: Every website. Assessed when pages were scanned and the scan recorded the three consent states.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Not Met earns 0 of 5 points. Weight 5: Core consent obligation; the scan observes it directly in the pre-consent state.

requirements.title: A consent mechanism is provided where tracking is used
observations: A consent mechanism (banner) was detected on the scanned pages.
requirements.description: A consent mechanism is provided wherever analytics or marketing tracking is used.
requirements.criteria: Met: a banner or consent tool was detected and displayed. Not Met: tracking was observed but no consent mechanism was found. Not Applicable: no analytics or marketing tracking was observed. Unable to Verify: a consent tool is loaded but its banner was not displayed to the scanner, no pages were scanned, or the page is a framed wrapper.
requirements.expected_evidence: Consent-mechanism detection (banner or consent tool) on the scanned pages, and whether its banner was displayed.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 1 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.applicability: Applies when analytics or marketing tracking is observed; otherwise Not Applicable.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Met earns 4 of 4 points. Weight 4: Prerequisite for valid consent; observed directly.

requirements.title: Refusing consent is honoured
observations: Reject was clicked and confirmed, and no analytics or marketing was observed afterwards.
requirements.description: When the visitor refuses consent, the refusal is honoured.
requirements.criteria: Met: Reject was clicked, the banner recorded it, and no known analytics or marketing activity was observed afterwards. Not Met: such activity was observed after a confirmed Reject. Unable to Verify: Reject could not be operated or confirmed, or the banner was not displayed. Not Applicable: no consent mechanism exists.
requirements.expected_evidence: The After Reject state, observed after a Reject click that the banner confirmed.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 1 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.applicability: Applies when a consent mechanism exists and Reject could be operated; otherwise Not Applicable or Unable to Verify.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Met earns 4 of 4 points. Weight 4: Consent that cannot be refused is not free; observed only when Reject was clicked and confirmed.

requirements.title: Refusing is as easy as accepting
observations: A consent banner was shown but no equally prominent reject-all option was found.
requirements.description: Refusing consent is as easy as giving it.
requirements.criteria: Met: a reject-all option was found alongside accept. Not Met: a banner was shown but no equally prominent reject-all option was found. Unable to Verify: the banner was not displayed or the option was not recorded. Not Applicable: no banner was found.
requirements.expected_evidence: The consent banner's options, as detected on the scanned pages.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 1 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.why_it_matters: The ease of withdrawing or refusing consent must be comparable to the ease of giving it (Act s.6(4); Rules r.3(c)(i)).
requirements.remediation: Add a reject-all control of the same prominence as accept, on the first layer of the banner.
requirements.verification: Re-scan: the banner shows a reject-all option on its first layer.
requirements.applicability: Applies when a consent banner is shown; otherwise Not Applicable.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Not Met earns 0 of 4 points. Weight 4: The Act requires withdrawal to be comparable in ease to giving consent; a reject-all option is the observable proxy.

human_review.statement: A website scan cannot establish complete DPDP compliance. It shows what the scanned pages did in this scan. A network request is not proof that a tracker ran, and a cookie or third-party request is not by itself a legal violation: the items below need business context or legal interpretation before they are treated as violations.

items.topic: Requests to known analytics or advertising services before consent
known: 1 request(s) or cookie(s) matching known analytics/marketing services were observed on the scanned pages before any consent interaction.
The browser contacted those services. This is evidence of a request, not proof that a tracker ran or of what it sent.
missing: Whether personal data was actually sent, and which.
The purpose each service serves for the business, and whether any of them is strictly necessary for the service the visitor asked for.
Whether the organisation relies on a ground other than consent (a legitimate use under the Act) for any of this processing.
items.decision: Decide, with legal advice, whether this processing needed consent and whether it was lawful without it. If it did, move the services behind consent and re-scan.

items.topic: Requirements that need organisational evidence
known: None of these can be observed through a public website scan: Contact of the Data Protection Officer or a responsible person is published; The means to exercise data principal rights are published; A grievance redressal system with a response period of at most 90 days is published; Reasonable security safeguards are in place; Personal data breaches are intimated to the Board and affected individuals.

This scan makes no statement about whether retention rules, a DPIA, grievance handling, breach response times, or a record of processing activities (ROPA) exist or are complete. A ROPA is not required by name under the DPDP Act or Rules; if the organisation keeps one, it is supporting evidence, not a scored check.
missing: Policies, procedures, logs, records and contact details held by the organisation.
items.decision: Provide the evidence for each, or assess it outside this scan.

items.topic: Which entity-specific duties apply to the organisation
known: These were excluded from the score because a website does not show them: Consent Manager registration and obligations; Erasure after the Third Schedule period, with 48 hours' notice; Verifiable parental or guardian consent for children's data; Significant Data Fiduciary duties (annual DPIA and audit).
missing: Whether the organisation processes children's data, is a notified Significant Data Fiduciary, is a Consent Manager, or falls in a Third Schedule class.
items.decision: Declare which apply, so they are included in the assessment.

items.topic: Most assessed duties are not yet in force
known: The consent and notice duties start on 2027-05-13 (18 months after the Rules were published). This assessment is a readiness view, not a statement that a duty is currently breached.
missing: Whether any transitional or sector-specific rule applies to this organisation.
items.decision: Use the findings to prepare, and confirm timing and applicability with legal advice.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

observations: 1 analytics/marketing cookie(s)/script(s) fired before any consent interaction.
requirements.description: Analytics and marketing cookies and scripts do not run before the visitor has given consent.
requirements.criteria: Met: no request or cookie matching a known analytics or marketing service was observed before any consent interaction. Partially Met: only unclassified third-party items fired before consent. Not Met: at least one known analytics or marketing request or cookie was observed before consent. Unable to Verify: no pages scanned, a framed wrapper, or no three-state consent record.

requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.

human_review.statement: A website scan cannot establish complete DPDP compliance. It shows what the scanned pages did in this scan. A network request is not proof that a tracker ran, and a cookie or third-party request is not by itself a legal violation: the items below need business context or legal interpretation before they are treated as violations.

items.topic: Requests to known analytics or advertising services before consent
known: 1 request(s) or cookie(s) matching known analytics/marketing services were observed on the scanned pages before any consent interaction.
The browser contacted those services. This is evidence of a request, not proof that a tracker ran or of what it sent.
missing: Whether personal data was actually sent, and which.
The purpose each service serves for the business, and whether any of them is strictly necessary for the service the visitor asked for.
Whether the organisation relies on a ground other than consent (a legitimate use under the Act) for any of this processing.
items.decision: Decide, with legal advice, whether this processing needed consent and whether it was lawful without it. If it did, move the services behind consent and re-scan.

items.topic: Requests or cookies that could not be classified
known: 1 request(s) or cookie(s) matched no known vendor signature, so the scan did not classify them (rule R-008).
missing: Their purpose and owner.
items.decision: Identify them. The scan does not treat them as violations.

items.topic: No privacy notice was found
known: No privacy policy page was found on the 5 main-domain page(s) scanned.
missing: Whether a notice exists elsewhere (another path, a pop-up, an app), and whether its content meets the notice requirements.
items.decision: Confirm where the notice is published and whether it is linked from every page that collects personal data.

items.topic: Only the first 5 pages of the main domain are assessed
known: 5 pages were scanned, which is the limit. Other pages of the main domain may behave differently.
missing: Behaviour on pages that were not scanned, such as sign-up, checkout or account pages.
items.decision: Scan a specific page directly if it matters (for example the one that collects personal data).

items.topic: Requirements that need organisational evidence
known: None of these can be observed through a public website scan: Contact of the Data Protection Officer or a responsible person is published; The means to exercise data principal rights are published; A grievance redressal system with a response period of at most 90 days is published; Reasonable security safeguards are in place; Personal data breaches are intimated to the Board and affected individuals.

This scan makes no statement about whether retention rules, a DPIA, grievance handling, breach response times, or a record of processing activities (ROPA) exist or are complete. A ROPA is not required by name under the DPDP Act or Rules; if the organisation keeps one, it is supporting evidence, not a scored check.
missing: Policies, procedures, logs, records and contact details held by the organisation.
items.decision: Provide the evidence for each, or assess it outside this scan.

items.topic: Which entity-specific duties apply to the organisation
known: These were excluded from the score because a website does not show them: Consent Manager registration and obligations; Erasure after the Third Schedule period, with 48 hours' notice; Verifiable parental or guardian consent for children's data; Significant Data Fiduciary duties (annual DPIA and audit).
missing: Whether the organisation processes children's data, is a notified Significant Data Fiduciary, is a Consent Manager, or falls in a Third Schedule class.
items.decision: Declare which apply, so they are included in the assessment.

items.topic: Most assessed duties are not yet in force
known: The consent and notice duties start on 2027-05-13 (18 months after the Rules were published). This assessment is a readiness view, not a statement that a duty is currently breached.
missing: Whether any transitional or sector-specific rule applies to this organisation.
items.decision: Use the findings to prepare, and confirm timing and applicability with legal advice.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

observations: 1 analytics/marketing cookie(s)/script(s) fired before any consent interaction.
requirements.description: Analytics and marketing cookies and scripts do not run before the visitor has given consent.
requirements.criteria: Met: no request or cookie matching a known analytics or marketing service was observed before any consent interaction. Partially Met: only unclassified third-party items fired before consent. Not Met: at least one known analytics or marketing request or cookie was observed before consent. Unable to Verify: no pages scanned, a framed wrapper, or no three-state consent record.
requirements.expected_evidence: Before-consent observations (requests and cookies, with the page) from a scan pass made before any banner interaction.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 3 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.why_it_matters: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action (Act s.6(1)). Processing that starts before that choice has no consent behind it unless another ground in the Act applies.
requirements.remediation: Load analytics and marketing tags only after the visitor accepts: configure the consent tool to block them by default, or start them from its accept callback. Identify each unclassified item and treat it as non-essential unless it is needed for the service the visitor asked for.
requirements.verification: Re-scan. The Before Consent state should show no analytics or marketing requests or cookies, and they should appear only after Accept.
requirements.applicability: Every website. Assessed when pages were scanned and the scan recorded the three consent states.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Not Met earns 0 of 5 points. Weight 5: Core consent obligation; the scan observes it directly in the pre-consent state.

verified_gaps.title: No analytics or marketing processing before consent
what_the_scan_observed: 1 analytics/marketing cookie(s)/script(s) fired before any consent interaction.
verified_gaps.why_it_matters: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action (Act s.6(1)). Processing that starts before that choice has no consent behind it unless another ground in the Act applies.
verified_gaps.recommended_action: Load analytics and marketing tags only after the visitor accepts: configure the consent tool to block them by default, or start them from its accept callback. human_review.statement: A website scan cannot establish complete DPDP compliance. It shows what the scanned pages did in this scan. A network request is not proof that a tracker ran, and a cookie or third-party request is not by itself a legal violation: the items below need business context or legal interpretation before they are treated as violations.

items.topic: Requests to known analytics or advertising services before consent
known: 1 request(s) or cookie(s) matching known analytics/marketing services were observed on the scanned pages before any consent interaction.
The browser contacted those services. This is evidence of a request, not proof that a tracker ran or of what it sent.
missing: Whether personal data was actually sent, and which.
The purpose each service serves for the business, and whether any of them is strictly necessary for the service the visitor asked for.
Whether the organisation relies on a ground other than consent (a legitimate use under the Act) for any of this processing.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

requirements.title: No analytics or marketing processing before consent
observations: 1 analytics/marketing cookie(s)/script(s) fired before any consent interaction.
requirements.description: Analytics and marketing cookies and scripts do not run before the visitor has given consent.
requirements.criteria: Met: no request or cookie matching a known analytics or marketing service was observed before any consent interaction. Partially Met: only unclassified third-party items fired before consent. Not Met: at least one known analytics or marketing request or cookie was observed before consent. Unable to Verify: no pages scanned, a framed wrapper, or no three-state consent record.
requirements.expected_evidence: Before-consent observations (requests and cookies, with the page) from a scan pass made before any banner interaction.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 3 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.why_it_matters: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action (Act s.6(1)). Processing that starts before that choice has no consent behind it unless another ground in the Act applies.
requirements.remediation: Load analytics and marketing tags only after the visitor accepts: configure the consent tool to block them by default, or start them from its accept callback. Identify each unclassified item and treat it as non-essential unless it is needed for the service the visitor asked for.
requirements.verification: Re-scan. The Before Consent state should show no analytics or marketing requests or cookies, and they should appear only after Accept.
requirements.applicability: Every website. Assessed when pages were scanned and the scan recorded the three consent states.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Not Met earns 0 of 8 points. Weight 8 (configured; documented default 5): Core consent obligation; the scan observes it directly in the pre-consent state.

requirements.title: A consent mechanism is provided where tracking is used
observations: A consent mechanism (banner) was detected on the scanned pages.
requirements.description: A consent mechanism is provided wherever analytics or marketing tracking is used.
requirements.criteria: Met: a banner or consent tool was detected and displayed. Not Met: tracking was observed but no consent mechanism was found. Not Applicable: no analytics or marketing tracking was observed. Unable to Verify: a consent tool is loaded but its banner was not displayed to the scanner, no pages were scanned, or the page is a framed wrapper.
requirements.expected_evidence: Consent-mechanism detection (banner or consent tool) on the scanned pages, and whether its banner was displayed.
requirements.sufficiency_reason: Direct observation on the scanned pages.
requirements.limitation: Covers only the 3 main-domain page(s) scanned.
requirements.applicability: Applies when analytics or marketing tracking is observed; otherwise Not Applicable.
requirements.scoring_rationale: Met earns 4 of 4 points. Weight 4: Prerequisite for valid consent; observed directly.

requirements.title: Refusing consent is honoured
observations: Reject was clicked and confirmed, and no analytics or marketing was observed afterwards.

human_review.statement: A website scan cannot establish complete DPDP compliance. It shows what the scanned pages did in this scan. A network request is not proof that a tracker ran, and a cookie or third-party request is not by itself a legal violation: the items below need business context or legal interpretation before they are treated as violations.

items.topic: Requests to known analytics or advertising services before consent
known: 1 request(s) or cookie(s) matching known analytics/marketing services were observed on the scanned pages before any consent interaction.
The browser contacted those services. This is evidence of a request, not proof that a tracker ran or of what it sent.
missing: Whether personal data was actually sent, and which.
The purpose each service serves for the business, and whether any of them is strictly necessary for the service the visitor asked for.
Whether the organisation relies on a ground other than consent (a legitimate use under the Act) for any of this processing.
items.decision: Decide, with legal advice, whether this processing needed consent and whether it was lawful without it. If it did, move the services behind consent and re-scan.

items.topic: Requirements that need organisational evidence
known: None of these can be observed through a public website scan: Contact of the Data Protection Officer or a responsible person is published; The means to exercise data principal rights are published; A grievance redressal system with a response period of at most 90 days is published; Reasonable security safeguards are in place; Personal data breaches are intimated to the Board and affected individuals.

This scan makes no statement about whether retention rules, a DPIA, grievance handling, breach response times, or a record of processing activities (ROPA) exist or are complete. A ROPA is not required by name under the DPDP Act or Rules; if the organisation keeps one, it is supporting evidence, not a scored check.
missing: Policies, procedures, logs, records and contact details held by the organisation.
items.decision: Provide the evidence for each, or assess it outside this scan.

items.topic: Which entity-specific duties apply to the organisation
known: These were excluded from the score because a website does not show them: Consent Manager registration and obligations; Erasure after the Third Schedule period, with 48 hours' notice; Verifiable parental or guardian consent for children's data; Significant Data Fiduciary duties (annual DPIA and audit).
missing: Whether the organisation processes children's data, is a notified Significant Data Fiduciary, is a Consent Manager, or falls in a Third Schedule class.
items.decision: Declare which apply, so they are included in the assessment.

items.topic: Most assessed duties are not yet in force
known: The consent and notice duties start on 2027-05-13 (18 months after the Rules were published). This assessment is a readiness view, not a statement that a duty is currently breached.
missing: Whether any transitional or sector-specific rule applies to this organisation.
items.decision: Use the findings to prepare, and confirm timing and applicability with legal advice.

methodology.weights_note: CUSTOM weights are in use for: DPDP-C1 = 8 (default 5). Scores made with different weights are not comparable.
methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

methodology.score_formula: DPDP Compliance Score (%) = (weighted points earned ÷ weighted points assessed) × 100
methodology.coverage_formula: Assessment coverage (%) = (weight of assessed requirements ÷ weight of applicable requirements) × 100. It is shown separately from the score: a high score with low coverage is not a reliable result.
points_rules: Met earns 100% of the requirement's weight, only when the evidence meets its written criteria.
Partially Met earns 50%, only when the evidence supports part of the requirement.
Not Met earns 0%, only when sufficient evidence supports an identified gap.
Unable to Verify and Not Applicable earn nothing and are left out of the denominator; Unable to Verify lowers coverage and is never counted as met or as not met.
methodology.reliability_rule: A score is shown only when at least 2 requirements were assessed and coverage is at least 30%. Otherwise the result is "Insufficient Evidence".
methodology.duplicate_rule: Each requirement is scored once, however many requests, cookies or pages relate to it. Where two requirements describe the same underlying gap, only the heavier one is penalised and the other is Not Applicable with the reason.
methodology.timing_rule: Requirements not yet in force are scored as readiness and shown as Future Readiness, never as current violations. A separate in-force score covers only duties already in force.
methodology.scope_rule: Only the entered main domain, up to 5 pages. Other websites are not assessed.

weights.title: No analytics or marketing processing before consent
weights.rationale: Core consent obligation; the scan observes it directly in the pre-consent state.
weights.applicability: Every website. Assessed when pages were scanned and the scan recorded the three consent states.

weights.title: A consent mechanism is provided where tracking is used
weights.rationale: Prerequisite for valid consent; observed directly.
weights.applicability: Applies when analytics or marketing tracking is observed; otherwise Not Applicable.

weights.title: Refusing consent is honoured
weights.rationale: Consent that cannot be refused is not free; observed only when Reject was clicked and confirmed.
weights.applicability: Applies when a consent mechanism exists and Reject could be operated; otherwise Not Applicable or Unable to Verify.

weights.title: Refusing is as easy as accepting
weights.rationale: The Act requires withdrawal to be comparable in ease to giving consent; a reject-all option is the observable proxy.
weights.applicability: Applies when a consent banner is shown; otherwise Not Applicable.

weights.title: Choices are specific to each purpose
weights.rationale: Consent must be specific; per-purpose choices are a supporting signal and a banner design, not a standalone breach.
weights.applicability: Applies when a consent banner is shown; otherwise Not Applicable.

weights.title: A privacy notice is published
weights.rationale: Notice must precede consent; the scan observes whether a policy page exists, not whether its content is adequate.
weights.applicability: Every website.

weights.title: Cookies and trackers are disclosed
weights.rationale: Notice must itemise the personal data processed; a dedicated cookie policy is the observable proxy.
weights.applicability: Applies when analytics or marketing tracking is observed; otherwise Not Applicable.

weights.title: Contact of the Data Protection Officer or a responsible person is published
weights.rationale: Statutory duty; the scan does not read policy text.
weights.applicability: Every data fiduciary. A business check: the organisation must supply the evidence.

weights.title: The means to exercise data principal rights are published
weights.rationale: Statutory duty; the scan does not read policy text.
weights.applicability: Every data fiduciary. A business check: the organisation must supply the evidence.

weights.title: A grievance redressal system with a response period of at most 90 days is published
weights.rationale: Statutory duty; the scan does not read policy text.
weights.applicability: Every data fiduciary. A business check: the organisation must supply the evidence.

weights.title: Reasonable security safeguards are in place
weights.rationale: Statutory duty; the scan cannot see an organisation's internal controls.
weights.applicability: Every data fiduciary. A business check: the organisation must supply the evidence.

weights.title: Personal data breaches are intimated to the Board and affected individuals
weights.rationale: Statutory duty; the scan cannot see an organisation's incident process.
weights.applicability: Every data fiduciary. A business check: the organisation must supply the evidence, including its breach response times.

weights.title: Consent Manager registration and obligations
weights.rationale: Applies only to a registered Consent Manager.
weights.applicability: Only a registered Consent Manager. Included only when declared applicable.

weights.title: Erasure after the Third Schedule period, with 48 hours' notice
weights.rationale: Applies only to the classes in the Third Schedule (large e-commerce, online gaming, social media).
weights.applicability: Only the Third Schedule classes (large e-commerce, online gaming, social media). Included only when declared applicable.

weights.title: Verifiable parental or guardian consent for children's data
weights.rationale: Applies only where the organisation processes children's personal data.
weights.applicability: Only where the organisation processes children's personal data. Included only when declared applicable.

weights.title: Significant Data Fiduciary duties (annual DPIA and audit)
weights.rationale: Applies only to a notified Significant Data Fiduciary.
weights.applicability: Only a notified Significant Data Fiduciary. Included only when declared applicable.

categories.name: Consent
categories.rationale: The core of the Act's consent duty and the part of it a website scan can observe directly, so it carries the most weight.

categories.name: Notice
categories.rationale: Notice must precede consent. A scan can see whether a notice exists but not whether its content is adequate, so it carries less weight than consent.

categories.name: Data principal rights
categories.rationale: Statutory duties about rights and grievances. A scan cannot observe them; they are business checks.

categories.name: Security and breach
categories.rationale: Statutory safeguards and breach duties. A scan cannot observe them; they are business checks.
